'''Giuseppe Suzzi''' (1701<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-7svAAAAYAAJ&q=Giuseppe+Suzzi&pg=PA163|title=Della letteratura veneziana del secolo XVIII fino a'nostri giorni opera di Giannantonio Moschini|last=|first=|publisher=stamperia Palese|year=1806|isbn=|location=|pages=163}}</ref> - 5 January 1764) was an Italian [[mathematician]] and [[abbot]].<ref name="Friulani">{{Cite web|url=http://www.dizionariobiograficodeifriulani.it/suzzi-giuseppe/|title=Giuseppe Suzzi on Dizionario biografico dei Friulani}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ldbGocOPl2AC&q=Giuseppe+Suzzi&pg=PA440|title=Opere del conte Jacopo Riccati nobile Trevigiano. Tomo primo|last=|first=|publisher=appersso Jacopo Giusti|year=1761|isbn=|location=Lucca|pages=440}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://mathematica.sns.it/autori/1349/|title=Mathematica Italiana}}</ref>

== Life ==
Born in [[Ragogna]], [[province of Udine]], he studied in [[Udine]] and later in [[Murano]], [[Venice]], in the [[seminary]] of [[Somaschi Fathers]], where he was a relevant student of [[Giovanni Francesco Crivelli]].<ref name="Friulani" /> In 1722 he moved to the [[University of Padua]], when he also took lessons from [[Jacopo Riccati]] privately with Lodovico da Riva. These lessons were published in 1761 in a posthumous book by Riccati, with the solutions of many problems by Suzzi.<ref name="Friulani" /> Suzzi, an abbey, published many books on mathematical analysis and in 1744 he became professor of [[natural history]] in Padua, where he taught mainly within the tradition of [[aristotelianism]], but also giving space to newer philosophical ideas.<ref name="Friulani" /> In 1750 he became a member of the Accademia dei Ricovrati in Padua (later [[Accademia galileiana di scienze, lettere ed arti]]). He retired from University in 1762 and died in Venice 5 January 1764.<ref name="Friulani" />
